_comment: GENERATED by scripts/analytics/catalogue.mjs from spa/src/analytics/catalogue/. Do not hand-edit: `make analytics-catalogue-check` compares this byte for byte with what the TypeScript source renders right now.

boot.index.fetch.what: the boot-video index was fetched and merged onto the catalog

boot.video.played.what: a boot video actually started playing in front of somebody

fleet.faceted.what: a human filtered the fleet table by a column facet

fleet.searched.what: a human typed in the fleet free-text filter

fleet.sorted.what: a human sorted the fleet table by some column

fleet.usage.fetch.what: the per-station interaction totals were fetched from the server

fleet.usage.shown.what: at least one row rendered with real usage numbers in it, in a visible tab

fleet.usage.sorted.what: a human sorted the fleet BY the usage column — the strongest evidence the fetch earns its keep

keyboard.osk.used.what: a key was pressed on the ON-SCREEN keyboard, not a physical one

station.key.used.what: a key went down on a live guest

station.pointer.used.what: a button went down on a live guest

stream.overlay.shown.what: the Cmd/Ctrl+N diagnostic overlay was actually on screen

stream.stats.polled.what: a station session started polling live stream stats for the debug overlay

walkin.play.claimInstant.what: a claim was answered with a clone immediately — the pool had a free machine for this visitor

walkin.play.claimQueued.what: a claim was answered with a queue position — every clone of that station was taken at that moment

walkin.register.refused.what: a stranger reached the walk-in door while access was closed and was shown the closed sentence

keyboard.compose.what: typing something at a guest with the on-screen keyboard sheet

station.connect.what: opening a station and getting a first frame out of it

walkin.play.what: claiming a private clone and getting a machine the visitor actually drives

walkin.register.what: a stranger with no account getting one and reaching a machine to play

fleet.find.hScrollReversals.what: a high value means people overshoot and backtrack — they cannot predict where a column is

fleet.find.hScrollScreens.what: a high value means the columns people want are far from the ones they land on

keyboard.compose.correctionsPct.what: a high value means this machine's hand-written key layout puts keys where people do not expect them, so the profile data is wrong and worth fixing before adding another

keyboard.compose.layerSwitches.what: a high value means the characters people need are spread across layers, so the split is costing more round trips than it saves screen space

keyboard.compose.toFirstKeyMs.what: a high value means the keyboard comes up and the key people came for is not findable at a glance, so the layout needs reordering rather than more keys

station.open.toFirstFrameMs.what: a high value means visitors stare at a spinner between choosing a machine and seeing it

walkin.play.claimRetries.what: a high value means one press of Play does not get a machine, so the queue card is doing work the pool should be doing

walkin.play.queueMs.what: a high value means visitors who meet a full pool wait long enough to give up, which is the argument for raising poolSize past 3

walkin.play.toPlayableMs.what: a high value means the gap between being handed a clone and being able to use it is where walk-ins are lost, so the resume path is worth more than the claim path

walkin.register.exhibitPickMs.what: a high value means a visitor who already has an account still cannot choose between the three cards, so the cards are not telling the machines apart

walkin.register.hesitationMs.what: a high value means the walk-in page does not tell an arriving stranger what to do — rewrite the lede and the call to action before optimising anything downstream

walkin.register.landingMs.what: a high value means the landing page is where registrations stall, so shortening it beats speeding up anything after it

walkin.register.passkeyMs.what: a high value means the platform passkey ceremony is where the door spends its time, so the fix is preparing the visitor for it rather than changing our copy

walkin.register.passkeyRetries.what: a high value means passkey enrolment is failing for platform reasons visitors cannot fix, so the door needs a diagnosable failure path rather than better wording
